correctness.rationale: The source's original diffusion is sigma_i(t,N_i)N_i, while Section 4 changes it to sigma_i(t,N_i)(N_i-N_i*). Substitution of U_i=N_i-N_i* into the original equations leaves nonzero constant diffusion at U=0 in every one of the four source cases when epsilon,delta>0. A constant Itô equilibrium requires zero diffusion. Itô's formula gives the exact right derivative of E||N_t-P*||^2 at t=0 as ||G(P*)||^2, yielding the four stated positive coefficients. The equilibrium and all numerical coefficients were replayed exactly from the source parameters.

value.rationale: The source's principal theoretical conclusion is that small stochastic immigration preserves stability. The model switch shows that this conclusion is not proved for the actual immigration equations: their positive deterministic equilibrium ceases to be a stochastic point equilibrium as soon as immigration noise is nonzero. The four exact short-time departure rates quantify the gap at the paper's own benchmark, separating legitimate stationary-fluctuation questions from an inapplicable point-stability theorem.
